messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Zepbound and Mounjaro contain the same active ingredient, tirzepatide, and share the same inactive ingredients.
Active ingredient: tirzepatide
Inactive ingredients (single-dose pens and vials):
Sodium chloride
Sodium phosphate dibasic heptahydrate
Water for injection
Hydrochloric acid and/or sodium hydroxide (added to adjust pH)
Additional inactive ingredients (KwikPen and multi-dose vial only):
Benzyl alcohol
Glycerin
Phenol
Triplet: ["Zepbound", "shares inactive ingredients with", "Mounjaro"]

The relation 'shares inactive ingredients with' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug has the same inactive components as the drug specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'has inactive ingredient': The subject drug contains the inactive pharmaceutical ingredient specified by the object entity.
B. 'contains ingredient': The subject drug product contains the active ingredient specified by the object entity.
C. 'has same risk as': The subject drug has the same risk or adverse effect as the object entity.
D. 'has same doses as': The subject drug is available in the same dose amounts as the object drug.
E. 'similar to': The subject drug is related to or an alternative for the drug specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
